fields.label: Navigates beyond inland, sheltered and port-regulated waters
fields.help: Select Yes if the vessel’s navigation extends beyond the waters excluded from the definition in Article II(1)(i).

fields.label: Ordinarily engaged in commercial activity
fields.help: Article II(4) covers ordinarily commercial operations regardless of public or private ownership.

fields.label: Engaged in fishing or similar pursuits
fields.help: Article II(4) expressly excludes these activities.

fields.label: Ship of traditional build under Article II(4)
fields.help: The treaty gives dhows and junks as examples of traditional builds.

fields.label: Warship or naval auxiliary
fields.help: Article II(4) expressly excludes these ships.

fields.label: International voyage under Regulation 5.1.3
fields.help: For this regulation the voyage must be from a country to a port outside that country.

fields.label: Operating from or between ports in another country
fields.help: Regulation 5.1.3(1)(b) also covers a participating flag’s ship operating from a port or between ports in a different country.

fields.label: Shipowner requested MLC certification
fields.help: Under Regulation 5.1.3(2) the shipowner may request certification from the member whose flag the vessel flies.

sections.title: Gross tonnage
sections.text:
(c)   gross tonnage means the gross tonnage calculated in accordance with the ton-
     nage measurement regulations contained in Annex I to the International Conven-
      tion on Tonnage Measurement of Ships, 1969, or any successor Convention; for
      ships covered by the tonnage measurement interim scheme adopted by the Inter-
      national Maritime Organization, the gross tonnage is that which is included in the

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Consult the tonnage certificate and the treaty definition.

sections.title: Meaning of ship and the waters excluded

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Read the full application provisions in Article II(4)–(6).

sections.title: Commercial ships and excluded ship types
sections.text:
4.  Except as expressly provided otherwise, this Convention applies to all ships,
whether publicly or privately owned, ordinarily engaged in commercial activities, other
than ships engaged in fishing or in similar pursuits and ships of traditional build such
as dhows and junks. This Convention does not apply to warships or naval auxiliaries.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Article II(5) gives the competent authority a role where application is in doubt.

sections.title: Competent authority determination in case of doubt
sections.text:
5.   In the event of doubt as to whether this Convention applies to a ship or par-
ticular category of ships, the question shall be determined by the competent authority
in each Member after consultation with the shipowners’ and seafarers’ organizations
concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Consult the competent authority if the status of a ship or category is in doubt.

sections.title: Limited national determination for smaller ships
sections.text:
6.  Where the competent authority determines that it would not be reasonable
or practicable at the present time to apply certain details of the Code referred to in
Article VI, paragraph 1, to a ship or particular categories of ships flying the flag of the
Member, the relevant provisions of the Code shall not apply to the extent that the subject

matter is dealt with differently by national laws or regulations or collective bargaining
agreements or other measures. Such a determination may only be made in consultation
with the shipowners’ and seafarers’ organizations concerned and may only be made with
respect to ships of less than 200 gross tonnage not engaged in international voyages.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The authority must make the determination and ensure alternative provision for particular Code details. These thresholds alone grant no exemption.

sections.title: Compulsory certification and the definition of international voyage
sections.text:
1.   This Regulation applies to ships of:
(a)   500 gross tonnage or over, engaged in international voyages; and
(b)  500 gross tonnage or over, flying the flag of a Member and operating from a port,
     or between ports, in another country.
For the purpose of this Regulation, “international voyage” means a voyage from a coun-
try to a port outside such a country.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The 500 GT threshold is inclusive. Either specified operating pattern satisfies paragraph 1.

sections.title: Certification at the shipowner’s request
sections.text:
2.   This Regulation also applies to any ship that flies the flag of a Member and
is not covered by paragraph 1 of this Regulation, at the request of the shipowner to the
Member concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Paragraph 2 concerns a ship outside paragraph 1 following its owner’s request to the flag member.

sections.title: Carriage and maintenance of the maritime labour certificate
sections.text:
3.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a mari-
time labour certificate certifying that the working and living conditions of seafarers on
the ship, including measures for ongoing compliance to be included in the declaration
of maritime labour compliance referred to in paragraph 4 of this Regulation, have been
inspected and meet the requirements of national laws or regulations or other measures
implementing this Convention.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The certificate duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

sections.title: Declaration of maritime labour compliance
sections.text:
4.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a
declaration of maritime labour compliance stating the national requirements implement-
ing this Convention for the working and living conditions for seafarers and setting out
the measures adopted by the shipowner to ensure compliance with the requirements
on the ship or ships concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The declaration duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

(a)   500 gross tonnage or over, engaged in international voyages; and
(b)  500 gross tonnage or over, flying the flag of a Member and operating from a port,
     or between ports, in another country.
For the purpose of this Regulation, “international voyage” means a voyage from a coun-
try to a port outside such a country.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The 500 GT threshold is inclusive. Either specified operating pattern satisfies paragraph 1.

sections.title: Certification at the shipowner’s request
sections.text:
2.   This Regulation also applies to any ship that flies the flag of a Member and
is not covered by paragraph 1 of this Regulation, at the request of the shipowner to the
Member concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Paragraph 2 concerns a ship outside paragraph 1 following its owner’s request to the flag member.

sections.title: Carriage and maintenance of the maritime labour certificate
sections.text:
3.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a mari-
time labour certificate certifying that the working and living conditions of seafarers on
the ship, including measures for ongoing compliance to be included in the declaration
of maritime labour compliance referred to in paragraph 4 of this Regulation, have been
inspected and meet the requirements of national laws or regulations or other measures
implementing this Convention.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The certificate duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

sections.title: Declaration of maritime labour compliance
sections.text:
4.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a
declaration of maritime labour compliance stating the national requirements implement-
ing this Convention for the working and living conditions for seafarers and setting out
the measures adopted by the shipowner to ensure compliance with the requirements
on the ship or ships concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The declaration duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

sections.text:

or practicable at the present time to apply certain details of the Code referred to in

Member, the relevant provisions of the Code shall not apply to the extent that the subject

matter is dealt with differently by national laws or regulations or collective bargaining
agreements or other measures. Such a determination may only be made in consultation
with the shipowners’ and seafarers’ organizations concerned and may only be made with
respect to ships of less than 200 gross tonnage not engaged in international voyages.

sections.title: Commercial ships and excluded ship types
sections.text:
4.  Except as expressly provided otherwise, this Convention applies to all ships,
whether publicly or privately owned, ordinarily engaged in commercial activities, other
than ships engaged in fishing or in similar pursuits and ships of traditional build such
as dhows and junks. This Convention does not apply to warships or naval auxiliaries.

sections.title: Competent authority determination in case of doubt
sections.text:
5.   In the event of doubt as to whether this Convention applies to a ship or par-
ticular category of ships, the question shall be determined by the competent authority
in each Member after consultation with the shipowners’ and seafarers’ organizations
concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Consult the competent authority if the status of a ship or category is in doubt.

sections.title: Limited national determination for smaller ships
sections.text:
6.  Where the competent authority determines that it would not be reasonable
or practicable at the present time to apply certain details of the Code referred to in
Article VI, paragraph 1, to a ship or particular categories of ships flying the flag of the
Member, the relevant provisions of the Code shall not apply to the extent that the subject

matter is dealt with differently by national laws or regulations or collective bargaining
agreements or other measures. Such a determination may only be made in consultation
with the shipowners’ and seafarers’ organizations concerned and may only be made with
respect to ships of less than 200 gross tonnage not engaged in international voyages.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The authority must make the determination and ensure alternative provision for particular Code details. These thresholds alone grant no exemption.

sections.title: Compulsory certification and the definition of international voyage
sections.text:
1.   This Regulation applies to ships of:
(a)   500 gross tonnage or over, engaged in international voyages; and
(b)  500 gross tonnage or over, flying the flag of a Member and operating from a port,
     or between ports, in another country.
For the purpose of this Regulation, “international voyage” means a voyage from a coun-
try to a port outside such a country.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The 500 GT threshold is inclusive. Either specified operating pattern satisfies paragraph 1.

sections.title: Certification at the shipowner’s request
sections.text:
2.   This Regulation also applies to any ship that flies the flag of a Member and
is not covered by paragraph 1 of this Regulation, at the request of the shipowner to the
Member concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Paragraph 2 concerns a ship outside paragraph 1 following its owner’s request to the flag member.

sections.title: Carriage and maintenance of the maritime labour certificate
sections.text:
3.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a mari-
time labour certificate certifying that the working and living conditions of seafarers on
the ship, including measures for ongoing compliance to be included in the declaration
of maritime labour compliance referred to in paragraph 4 of this Regulation, have been
inspected and meet the requirements of national laws or regulations or other measures
implementing this Convention.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The certificate duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

sections.title: Declaration of maritime labour compliance
sections.text:
4.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a
declaration of maritime labour compliance stating the national requirements implement-
ing this Convention for the working and living conditions for seafarers and setting out
the measures adopted by the shipowner to ensure compliance with the requirements
on the ship or ships concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The declaration duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

sections.title: Gross tonnage
sections.text:
(c)   gross tonnage means the gross tonnage calculated in accordance with the ton-
     nage measurement regulations contained in Annex I to the International Conven-
      tion on Tonnage Measurement of Ships, 1969, or any successor Convention; for
      ships covered by the tonnage measurement interim scheme adopted by the Inter-
      national Maritime Organization, the gross tonnage is that which is included in the
   REMARKS column of the International Tonnage Certificate (1969);

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Consult the tonnage certificate and the treaty definition.

sections.title: Meaning of ship and the waters excluded

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Read the full application provisions in Article II(4)–(6).

sections.title: Commercial ships and excluded ship types
sections.text:
4.  Except as expressly provided otherwise, this Convention applies to all ships,
whether publicly or privately owned, ordinarily engaged in commercial activities, other
than ships engaged in fishing or in similar pursuits and ships of traditional build such
as dhows and junks. This Convention does not apply to warships or naval auxiliaries.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Article II(5) gives the competent authority a role where application is in doubt.

sections.title: Competent authority determination in case of doubt
sections.text:
5.   In the event of doubt as to whether this Convention applies to a ship or par-
ticular category of ships, the question shall be determined by the competent authority
in each Member after consultation with the shipowners’ and seafarers’ organizations
concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Consult the competent authority if the status of a ship or category is in doubt.

sections.title: Limited national determination for smaller ships
sections.text:
6.  Where the competent authority determines that it would not be reasonable
or practicable at the present time to apply certain details of the Code referred to in
Article VI, paragraph 1, to a ship or particular categories of ships flying the flag of the
Member, the relevant provisions of the Code shall not apply to the extent that the subject

matter is dealt with differently by national laws or regulations or collective bargaining
agreements or other measures. Such a determination may only be made in consultation
with the shipowners’ and seafarers’ organizations concerned and may only be made with
respect to ships of less than 200 gross tonnage not engaged in international voyages.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The authority must make the determination and ensure alternative provision for particular Code details. These thresholds alone grant no exemption.

sections.title: Compulsory certification and the definition of international voyage
sections.text:
1.   This Regulation applies to ships of:
(a)   500 gross tonnage or over, engaged in international voyages; and
(b)  500 gross tonnage or over, flying the flag of a Member and operating from a port,
     or between ports, in another country.
For the purpose of this Regulation, “international voyage” means a voyage from a coun-
try to a port outside such a country.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The 500 GT threshold is inclusive. Either specified operating pattern satisfies paragraph 1.

sections.title: Certification at the shipowner’s request
sections.text:
2.   This Regulation also applies to any ship that flies the flag of a Member and
is not covered by paragraph 1 of this Regulation, at the request of the shipowner to the
Member concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Paragraph 2 concerns a ship outside paragraph 1 following its owner’s request to the flag member.

sections.title: Carriage and maintenance of the maritime labour certificate
sections.text:
3.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a mari-
time labour certificate certifying that the working and living conditions of seafarers on
the ship, including measures for ongoing compliance to be included in the declaration
of maritime labour compliance referred to in paragraph 4 of this Regulation, have been
inspected and meet the requirements of national laws or regulations or other measures
implementing this Convention.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The certificate duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

sections.title: Declaration of maritime labour compliance
sections.text:
4.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a
declaration of maritime labour compliance stating the national requirements implement-
ing this Convention for the working and living conditions for seafarers and setting out
the measures adopted by the shipowner to ensure compliance with the requirements
on the ship or ships concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The declaration duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

(a)   500 gross tonnage or over, engaged in international voyages; and
(b)  500 gross tonnage or over, flying the flag of a Member and operating from a port,
     or between ports, in another country.
For the purpose of this Regulation, “international voyage” means a voyage from a coun-
try to a port outside such a country.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The 500 GT threshold is inclusive. Either specified operating pattern satisfies paragraph 1.

sections.title: Certification at the shipowner’s request
sections.text:
2.   This Regulation also applies to any ship that flies the flag of a Member and
is not covered by paragraph 1 of this Regulation, at the request of the shipowner to the
Member concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Paragraph 2 concerns a ship outside paragraph 1 following its owner’s request to the flag member.

sections.title: Carriage and maintenance of the maritime labour certificate
sections.text:
3.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a mari-
time labour certificate certifying that the working and living conditions of seafarers on
the ship, including measures for ongoing compliance to be included in the declaration
of maritime labour compliance referred to in paragraph 4 of this Regulation, have been
inspected and meet the requirements of national laws or regulations or other measures
implementing this Convention.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The certificate duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

sections.title: Declaration of maritime labour compliance
sections.text:
4.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a
declaration of maritime labour compliance stating the national requirements implement-
ing this Convention for the working and living conditions for seafarers and setting out
the measures adopted by the shipowner to ensure compliance with the requirements
on the ship or ships concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The declaration duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

6.  Where the competent authority determines that it would not be reasonable
or practicable at the present time to apply certain details of the Code referred to in
Article VI, paragraph 1, to a ship or particular categories of ships flying the flag of the
Member, the relevant provisions of the Code shall not apply to the extent that the subject

matter is dealt with differently by national laws or regulations or collective bargaining
agreements or other measures. Such a determination may only be made in consultation
with the shipowners’ and seafarers’ organizations concerned and may only be made with
respect to ships of less than 200 gross tonnage not engaged in international voyages.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The authority must make the determination and ensure alternative provision for particular Code details. These thresholds alone grant no exemption.

sections.title: Compulsory certification and the definition of international voyage
sections.text:
1.   This Regulation applies to ships of:
(a)   500 gross tonnage or over, engaged in international voyages; and
(b)  500 gross tonnage or over, flying the flag of a Member and operating from a port,
     or between ports, in another country.
For the purpose of this Regulation, “international voyage” means a voyage from a coun-
try to a port outside such a country.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The 500 GT threshold is inclusive. Either specified operating pattern satisfies paragraph 1.

sections.title: Certification at the shipowner’s request
sections.text:
2.   This Regulation also applies to any ship that flies the flag of a Member and
is not covered by paragraph 1 of this Regulation, at the request of the shipowner to the
Member concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Paragraph 2 concerns a ship outside paragraph 1 following its owner’s request to the flag member.

sections.title: Carriage and maintenance of the maritime labour certificate
sections.text:
3.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a mari-
time labour certificate certifying that the working and living conditions of seafarers on
the ship, including measures for ongoing compliance to be included in the declaration
of maritime labour compliance referred to in paragraph 4 of this Regulation, have been
inspected and meet the requirements of national laws or regulations or other measures
implementing this Convention.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The certificate duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

sections.title: Declaration of maritime labour compliance
sections.text:
4.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a
declaration of maritime labour compliance stating the national requirements implement-
ing this Convention for the working and living conditions for seafarers and setting out
the measures adopted by the shipowner to ensure compliance with the requirements
on the ship or ships concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The declaration duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

sections.title: Gross tonnage
sections.text:
(c)   gross tonnage means the gross tonnage calculated in accordance with the ton-
     nage measurement regulations contained in Annex I to the International Conven-
      tion on Tonnage Measurement of Ships, 1969, or any successor Convention; for
      ships covered by the tonnage measurement interim scheme adopted by the Inter-
      national Maritime Organization, the gross tonnage is that which is included in the
   REMARKS column of the International Tonnage Certificate (1969);

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Consult the tonnage certificate and the treaty definition.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Read the full application provisions in Article II(4)–(6).

sections.title: Commercial ships and excluded ship types
sections.text:
4.  Except as expressly provided otherwise, this Convention applies to all ships,
whether publicly or privately owned, ordinarily engaged in commercial activities, other
than ships engaged in fishing or in similar pursuits and ships of traditional build such
as dhows and junks. This Convention does not apply to warships or naval auxiliaries.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Article II(5) gives the competent authority a role where application is in doubt.

sections.title: Competent authority determination in case of doubt
sections.text:
5.   In the event of doubt as to whether this Convention applies to a ship or par-
ticular category of ships, the question shall be determined by the competent authority
in each Member after consultation with the shipowners’ and seafarers’ organizations
concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Consult the competent authority if the status of a ship or category is in doubt.

sections.title: Limited national determination for smaller ships
sections.text:
6.  Where the competent authority determines that it would not be reasonable
or practicable at the present time to apply certain details of the Code referred to in
Article VI, paragraph 1, to a ship or particular categories of ships flying the flag of the
Member, the relevant provisions of the Code shall not apply to the extent that the subject

matter is dealt with differently by national laws or regulations or collective bargaining
agreements or other measures. Such a determination may only be made in consultation
with the shipowners’ and seafarers’ organizations concerned and may only be made with
respect to ships of less than 200 gross tonnage not engaged in international voyages.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The authority must make the determination and ensure alternative provision for particular Code details. These thresholds alone grant no exemption.

sections.title: Compulsory certification and the definition of international voyage
sections.text:
1.   This Regulation applies to ships of:
(a)   500 gross tonnage or over, engaged in international voyages; and
(b)  500 gross tonnage or over, flying the flag of a Member and operating from a port,
     or between ports, in another country.
For the purpose of this Regulation, “international voyage” means a voyage from a coun-
try to a port outside such a country.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The 500 GT threshold is inclusive. Either specified operating pattern satisfies paragraph 1.

sections.title: Certification at the shipowner’s request
sections.text:
2.   This Regulation also applies to any ship that flies the flag of a Member and
is not covered by paragraph 1 of this Regulation, at the request of the shipowner to the
Member concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: Paragraph 2 concerns a ship outside paragraph 1 following its owner’s request to the flag member.

sections.title: Carriage and maintenance of the maritime labour certificate
sections.text:
3.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a mari-
time labour certificate certifying that the working and living conditions of seafarers on
the ship, including measures for ongoing compliance to be included in the declaration
of maritime labour compliance referred to in paragraph 4 of this Regulation, have been
inspected and meet the requirements of national laws or regulations or other measures
implementing this Convention.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The certificate duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.

sections.title: Declaration of maritime labour compliance
sections.text:
4.  Each Member shall require ships that fly its flag to carry and maintain a
declaration of maritime labour compliance stating the national requirements implement-
ing this Convention for the working and living conditions for seafarers and setting out
the measures adopted by the shipowner to ensure compliance with the requirements
on the ship or ships concerned.

all.source: Individual flag action in the cited treaty status register

sections.caveat: The declaration duty is screened together with the two application routes in paragraphs 1–2.
